To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the accuracy of gender prediction can be improved with feature engineering and deep learning.

(i) a simple combination of the two systems, i.e. the voting of classifiers, outperforms both the systems, (ii) the BLSTM network outperforms all the previous deep learning systems, (iii) a simple voting of classifiers outperforms the deep neural networks, and (iv) the BLSTM system is the best performing system on our data set.

(i) a combination of the proposed features, along with the existing ones can be used for improved classification of gender and (ii) BLSTM networks can be used for gender classification, which is a first-of-its-kind attempt in this direction
In summary, our research is concerned with
two important issues: (a) the use of novel and effective features for gender classification and (b) the use of deep learning for this task.

the development of two systems for gender classification of blog authors: a feature mining based system using a voting of machine learners and a deep learning based system using Bidirectional Long Short-Term Memory networks.
the development of novel feature engineering techniques and the first ever application of deep learning to the task of gender identification.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
our first approach, the feature engineering based system is better than our second approach, i.e. the deep learning based approach.
our first system outperforms previous feature mining systems while our second system outperforms all other deep learning based systems.
the proposed BLSTM model outperforms the state-of-the-art feature mining system and is competitive with the state-of-the art deep learning system on the task of gender identification of blog authors.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the first approach, using the novel feature engineering, performs better than the state-of-the-art feature engineering based model on the first data set while the deep learning model outperforms the state-of-the art deep learning system on the second data set.

we have developed a novel feature extraction based approach which outperforms the previous state-ofthe-art model on the same data set and also a deep learning system based on LSTMs which performs comparably to the state-of-the-art on the same data.
our first approach outperforms the previous best feature mining systems while our second deep learning approach outperforms all other previous deep learning approaches for this task.
The main takeaway from our work is that
, while feature engineering systems are able to outperform deep learning models on the smaller data set, the latter are more effective on the larger one.
while the feature engineering based system is more effective on smaller data sets, deep learning based systems are better suited for larger data sets.
the deep learning approach is more scalable and generalizable as it can be used on a larger data set without any significant drop in performance.
